title: Wire Trap
summary: A packet capture holds a file transfer split across TCP segments. Reassemble it.
briefing:
NebulaCorp's SOC captured traffic from a host suspected of exfiltrating data over plain HTTP. You have a raw packet capture (capture.pcap).

The interesting exchange is a single TCP conversation on port 80. The server's response body was transmitted across more than one TCP segment, so you cannot just read a single packet — you must reassemble the TCP stream to recover the full payload.

Open the capture in Wireshark, find the HTTP conversation, and use "Follow > TCP Stream" to reassemble it. The response body is Base64-encoded. Decode it to recover the flag.

(This is a real libpcap file. Tools: Wireshark, tshark, tcpflow, or scapy.)
objectives: Locate the TCP conversation on port 80
Follow the TCP stream to reassemble the response body

hints.title: Follow the stream
hints.text: In Wireshark: right-click any packet in the port-80 conversation > Follow > TCP Stream. Or on the CLI: tshark -r capture.pcap -q -z follow,tcp,raw,0

hints.title: Decode the body
hints.text: The HTTP response body (after the blank line) is Base64. Concatenate it (ignore line breaks) and run: echo "<b64>" | base64 -d

artifacts.description: Raw libpcap capture (Ethernet/IPv4/TCP). Open in Wireshark.
